YELLOW=$(c '249;226;175')  # dirty git / mid ctx

SRC="$HOME/.claude/skills"
DST="$REPO/claude/skills"
EXCLUDES=(
  --exclude='.DS_Store' --exclude='node_modules' --exclude='.git'

    echo "synced: $skill"
  else
    echo "skip (not found in ~/.claude/skills): $skill"

# Playwright Skill for Claude Code

**General-purpose browser automation as a Claude Skill**

A [Claude Skill](https://www.anthropic.com/blog/skills) that enables Claude to write and execute any Playwright automation on-the-fly - from simple page tests to complex multi-step flows. Packaged as a [Claude Code Plugin](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugins) for easy installation and distribution.

Claude autonomously decides when to use this skill based on your browser automation needs, loading only the minimal information required for your specific task.

Made using Claude Code.

## Features

- **Any Automation Task** - Claude writes custom code for your specific request, not limited to pre-built scripts
- **Visible Browser by Default** - See automation in real-time with `headless: false`
- **Zero Module Resolution Errors** - Universal executor ensures proper module access
- **Progressive Disclosure** - Concise SKILL.md with full API reference loaded only when needed
- **Safe Cleanup** - Smart temp file management without race conditions
- **Comprehensive Helpers** - Optional utility functions for common tasks

## Installation

This repository is structured as a [Claude Code Plugin](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugins) containing a skill. You can install it as either a **plugin** (recommended) or extract it as a **standalone skill**.

### Understanding the Structure

This repository uses the plugin format with a nested structure:

```
playwright-skill/              # Plugin root
├── .claude-plugin/           # Plugin metadata
└── skills/
    └── playwright-skill/     # The actual skill
        └── SKILL.md
```

Claude Code expects skills to be directly in folders under `.claude/skills/`, so manual installation requires extracting the nested skill folder.

---

### Option 1: Plugin Installation (Recommended)

Install via Claude Code's plugin system for automatic updates and team distribution:

```bash
# Add this repository as a marketplace
/plugin marketplace add lackeyjb/playwright-skill

# Install the plugin
/plugin install playwright-skill@playwright-skill

# Navigate to the skill directory and run setup
cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/playwright-skill/skills/playwright-skill
npm run setup
```

Verify installation by running `/help` to confirm the skill is available.

---

### Option 2: Standalone Skill Installation

To install as a standalone skill (without the plugin system), extract only the skill folder:

**Global Installation (Available Everywhere):**

```bash
# Clone to a temporary location
git clone https://github.com/lackeyjb/playwright-skill.git /tmp/playwright-skill-temp

# Copy only the skill folder to your global skills directory
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
cp -r /tmp/playwright-skill-temp/skills/playwright-skill ~/.claude/skills/

# Navigate to the skill and run setup
cd ~/.claude/skills/playwright-skill
npm run setup

# Clean up temporary files
rm -rf /tmp/playwright-skill-temp
```

**Project-Specific Installation:**

```bash
# Clone to a temporary location
git clone https://github.com/lackeyjb/playwright-skill.git /tmp/playwright-skill-temp

# Copy only the skill folder to your project
mkdir -p .claude/skills
cp -r /tmp/playwright-skill-temp/skills/playwright-skill .claude/skills/

# Navigate to the skill and run setup
cd .claude/skills/playwright-skill
npm run setup

# Clean up temporary files
rm -rf /tmp/playwright-skill-temp
```

**Why this structure?** The plugin format requires the `skills/` directory for organizing multiple skills within a plugin. When installing as a standalone skill, you only need the inner `skills/playwright-skill/` folder contents.

---

### Option 3: Download Release

1. Download and extract the latest release from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/lackeyjb/playwright-skill/releases)
2. Copy only the `skills/playwright-skill/` folder to:
   - Global: `~/.claude/skills/playwright-skill`
   - Project: `/path/to/your/project/.claude/skills/playwright-skill`
3. Navigate to the skill directory and run setup:
   ```bash
   cd ~/.claude/skills/playwright-skill  # or your project path

   ```

---

Run `/help` to confirm the skill is loaded, then ask Claude to perform a simple browser task like "Test if google.com loads".

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Debian/Ubuntu (including WSL) base dev packages for Angular frontend work.
set -euo pipefail

sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y build-essential curl wget unzip git ca-certificates gnupg lsb-release jq

# GitHub CLI (official SIGNED apt repo)
if ! command -v gh >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo mkdir -p -m 755 /etc/apt/keyrings
  wget -qO- https://cli.github.com/packages/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg \
    | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null
  sudo chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg
  echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/githubcli-archive-keyring.gpg] https://cli.github.com/packages stable main" \
    | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/github-cli.list >/dev/null
  sudo apt-get update
  sudo apt-get install -y gh
fi

# Azure CLI (Microsoft's SIGNED apt repo — no `curl | sudo bash`)
if ! command -v az >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  sudo mkdir -p -m 755 /etc/apt/keyrings
  curl -sLS https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc \
    | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  sudo chmod go+r /etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg
  AZ_DIST="$(lsb_release -cs 2>/dev/null || echo jammy)"
  echo "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/microsoft.gpg] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/azure-cli/ ${AZ_DIST} main" \
    | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/azure-cli.list >/dev/null
  sudo apt-get update
  sudo apt-get install -y azure-cli
fi

## Audit: `manndotfiles`

**What it is:** A [chezmoi](https://chezmoi.io)-managed dotfiles repo that bootstraps one dev environment across macOS, Linux/WSL, and native Windows — tuned specifically for Angular multi-frontend consulting work at Accenture. 11 commits, started 2026-06-26, most recently touched today. Every commit is co-authored by Claude (Opus 4.8), so this has been built iteratively as a Claude Code collaboration, not just a static config dump.

### Architecture
- **chezmoi** templates (`dot_*.tmpl`) generate the right `.zshrc`/`.gitconfig`/PowerShell profile per OS, driven by two prompts asked once and remembered: **machine type** (`personal`/`work`) and **git email**. Name is hardcoded (constant across machines).
- **`install/setup.sh`** (macOS/Linux/WSL) and **`install/setup.ps1`** (Windows) do the actual toolchain install, run *after* `chezmoi apply`. Both are idempotent and self-updating — re-running installs anything missing and upgrades everything else to latest.
- **Install policy is npm-first**: anything on npm (`@angular/cli`, `nx`, `newman`, etc. in `install/npm-globals.txt`) installs via npm on every OS since it's fresher than Homebrew/winget. Brew/winget/apt carry only tools with no npm distribution (`git`, `gh`, `fnm`, Azure CLI, `jq`, VS Code app).
- Node is managed by **fnm**, pnpm via **corepack**, monorepo tooling is **Nx** (Module Federation added per-project, not globally).

### Claude Code configuration (`claude/`)
This is the most directly relevant piece to me:
- **`settings.seed.json`**: default `effortLevel: "high"`, `tui: "fullscreen"`, a curated allowlist (npm/ng/tsc builds, most git ops, `gh pr`, read-only `vercel`, `brew list`, `pip3 list`) and only official `claude-plugins-official` plugins (frontend-design, context7, superpowers, code-review, github, feature-dev, code-simplifier, ralph-loop, typescript-lsp, commit-commands, security-guidance, figma, pr-review-toolkit, vercel, etc.) — third-party marketplaces were explicitly removed.
- A hand-rolled **status line** (`statusline-command.sh`) — 24-bit truecolor, minimal-mono style: model · effort (color-scaled) · dir · git branch/dirty-dot · context bar · 5h/7d usage bars. Redesigned earlier today, replacing a more verbose version.
- One vendored personal skill: `playwright-skill` (third-party, from `lackeyjb/playwright-skill` — browser automation, auto-detects dev servers, writes throwaway scripts to `/tmp`). A `sync-skills-to-repo.sh` script snapshots skills named in `skills.txt` back into the repo.

### Security / compliance posture (the interesting part)
The commit history shows a deliberate, multi-pass hardening effort for using this on Accenture client engagements:
- **History was reinitialized once already** — the initial commit message states it squashed prior history "to purge a hardcoded corporate email and a GCP project id."
- On `machine = work`: code-egress commands (`git push`, `gh api`, `gh repo`, `vercel deploy`, `commit-push-pr`) were **removed** from the auto-allow permission seed so they always prompt; Vercel CLI and Postman are skipped entirely; Claude Code is **not** npm-installed (uses Accenture's Enterprise no-training-tenant managed install instead); profile detection fails **closed to "work"** if it can't be confirmed.
- Azure CLI install moved from `curl | sudo bash` to Microsoft's signed apt repo.
- `.gitignore` is deliberately wide (`*.local`, `.env*`, `*.p12/.pfx/.jks/.keystore`, `.npmrc`, `.netrc`, `.kube/`, `id_*`, etc.) — the repo carries **zero secrets**; auth is redone per-machine via `gh auth login`/`az login`/`claude`.
- VS Code's built-in Copilot/AI chat is disabled (`chat.disableAIFeatures: true`) while the Claude Code extension stays — consistent with the README's note that Accenture's AI-tools policy is the reason ChatGPT/Gemini extensions were removed.

### Minor things worth flagging (not urgent, just noticed while reading)
1. **Skill-sync asymmetry**: `sync-skills-to-repo.sh` (skills → repo) uses `rsync --delete`, but `claude-setup.sh`'s reverse sync (repo → `~/.claude/skills`) uses plain `rsync -a`. If a skill is ever dropped from `skills.txt`, it won't be cleaned out of `~/.claude/skills` on re-run.
2. **VS Code settings/keybindings apply on Windows but not on macOS/Linux** — `setup.ps1` copies `vscode/settings.json`/`keybindings.json` into place; `setup.sh` only installs extensions from `vscode/extensions.txt`, never copies settings/keybindings. The README frames `vscode/` as a "fallback" behind Settings Sync, so this is likely intentional, but it means the fallback only actually works on Windows today.
3. **Hardening scope is "code-egress" only** — `git reset`, `git checkout`, and `git rebase` are still auto-allowed even on the work profile. That's defensible (they don't leak code anywhere) but they're locally destructive, so it's a residual gap if the intent was ever broader than "don't auto-ship code."

Happy to fix any of these if you want — otherwise, the repo is in solid shape and clearly reflects a lot of careful, already-iterated-on work.
